newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Italy seeks U.N. Council session on Albania.
newsitem.headline: Italy seeks U.N. Council session on Albania.

text.p: Italy as well as Albania on Thursday asked the U.N. Security Council to meet urgently on the Balkan state's slide into anarchy.

An Italian spokesman said a statement from the 15-member council might help calm the situation. In Albania, arms depots in the capital Tirana and several other towns were looted and people used the weapons to raid food warehouses for emergency stockpiles.
Council members are expected to consider Italy the request for an urgent meeting late on Thursday.

Italy wants the council to adopt a statement saying that it "requests all weapons and ammunitions seized by citizens" be returned immediately. It would appeal to Albanians to refrain from the use of violence and reach a peaceful solution.

The Italian statement would also urge all U.N. members and international organisations to help search for a peaceful solution to the Albanian crisis. It would call for an "urgent need to reopen all communication facilities in the country."
Diplomats in Rome said that Italy was evacuating some 400 foreign nationals, 330 of them Italians, from Albania.
